extracted.intended_audience: covered entities and their legal/compliance staff (health care providers, hospitals, payers, insurers, plan sponsors, pharmacy benefit managers), OCR commenters, and policy implementers
extracted.subtask_description: Final-rule definitions and scope guidance for HHS OCR's implementation of Section 1557 nondiscrimination obligations, describing what counts as a health program or activity, covered technologies and services, and standards for language and interpretation supports. Useful for covered entities, counsel, and compliance officers determining coverage and operational requirements under §92.4 and related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction applies regardless of physical site
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule's jurisdiction over a 'health program or activity' applies regardless of where the program or activity takes place and whether it can be said to take place at a physical site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a hospital receiving NIH grant must not discriminate in screening and recruitment activities wherever they occur (at the hospital, community health fairs, online, or at a researcher's home). OCR declines to add references to physical sites because jurisdiction follows the program/activity, not site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of clinical research within 'health program or activity'
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical research is included in the definition of 'health program or activity' and the term 'engage in health or clinical research' is added to paragraph (1)(iv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR supports including clinical research because it involves people and differs from laboratory research; inclusion does not change how research is designed, conducted, or funded under existing research norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted targeting/exclusion in research protocols with nondiscriminatory justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria in research protocols that target or exclude certain populations are permissible where nondiscriminatory justifications establish such criteria are appropriate with respect to subject health/safety, scientific study design, or the purpose of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with the 2016 Rule preamble; inclusion of research does not alter fundamental research design—targeting/exclusion must be justified on health/safety, scientific, or purpose grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope tied to receipt/administration of Federal financial assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule applies to health programs and activities that receive Federal financial assistance from HHS, or that are administered by HHS or a title I entity; it does not apply generally to programs unrelated to health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an entity is 'principally engaged' as set forth in paragraph (2), all operations of the covered entity must comply even if some operations are not health-related. OCR will analyze on a fact-specific basis whether an activity meets the definition of a health program or activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of 'health-related service' that indicate coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Though not exhaustive, 'health-related service' includes medical, dental, and pharmaceutical care; preventive health services; physical, occupational, or speech therapy; behavioral health care; clinical trials; and transportation to/from such services when necessary to facilitate access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples illustrate the kinds of services that would bring an activity within the rule when Federal financial assistance is received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit inclusion of State Medicaid, CHIP, and Basic Health Program
rubrics_metrics.description: State Medicaid programs, Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP), and the Basic Health Program are included in paragraph (2) as examples of entities 'principally engaged' in providing or administering health-related services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reinstates clarity from the 2016 Rule and reduces confusion about coverage of these State programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of group health plans (fact-specific analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Group health plans are not expressly listed in paragraph (2) but may be covered if they provide or administer group health coverage and receive Federal financial assistance; whether a group health plan is a recipient or subrecipient is determined by a fact-specific analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will not assume a group health plan is an indirect recipient merely because the employer receives Federal funds; recipient group health plans that receive Federal financial assistance are considered 'principally engaged' and all their operations would be covered. Many group health plans do not receive Federal financial assistance; coverage is fact-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer and plan sponsor liability limited (employment practices excluded)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers and plan sponsors are not subject to the rule with regard to their employment practices, pursuant to §92.2(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A group health plan does not automatically become a covered entity because its plan sponsor receives Federal assistance; single employers as plan sponsors do not become covered entities due to employment practices alone. See §92.2(b) discussion for employer liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractors and recipient covered entities may themselves be subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities that contract with a group health plan or otherwise perform health program functions could be subject to the rule themselves, regardless of the group health plan's liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: health insurance issuers offering coverage to a fully-insured group health plan or providing third-party administrator services for a self-funded plan may be covered if they receive Federal financial assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) and coverage analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to expressly list PBMs in paragraph (2), but recognizes that PBMs' activities (formulary development, networks, reimbursements, rebates, claims/appeals processing, utilization review) constitute operation of health programs and activities under section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PBMs receive Federal financial assistance or are principally engaged, all their operations are covered. If not directly funded, PBMs integrated with issuers or pharmacies might be covered as part of operations of a recipient; corporate-structure fact-specific analysis applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate-separateness factors for subsidiaries and related entities
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining whether parts of a recipient's operations are separate legal entities (and thus not subject to the rule), OCR may consider organizational structure and interrelatedness between entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant factors include degree of common ownership, management, and control; whether entities share centralized control of labor relations; whether the entity can accept/reject Federal funding or exercise controlling authority over a federally funded program; and whether the purpose of separation was to avoid liability or civil rights requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of information and communication technology (ICT)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICT means information technology and other equipment, systems, technologies, or processes whose principal function is creation, manipulation, storage, display, receipt, or transmission of electronic data and information, as well as any associated content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR provided examples in the proposed definition and notes EHRs meet the definition but need not be listed explicitly in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language assistance services definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Language assistance services include, but are not limited to: (1) oral language assistance (interpretation in non-English languages, in-person or remotely, by a qualified interpreter, including qualified bilingual/multilingual staff), (2) written translation by a qualified translator of written content into/from other languages, and (3) written notice of availability of language assistance services (taglines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition is non-exhaustive and works with §92.201 requirements that covered entities must take reasonable steps to provide meaningful access to individuals with LEP. Assistance with form completion is not added to the definition but covered entities must provide language assistance consistent with §92.201 when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology: 'individual with limited English proficiency' adopted
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR replaces the term 'limited English proficient individual' with 'individual with limited English proficiency' throughout §92.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition retains emphasis that individuals may be competent in some communicative functions and still need translation for others; OCR declines to broaden the definition to include persons whose primary language is English but who have limited English ability, citing the statute's reliance on national origin discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine translation definition and review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Machine translation is defined as automated translation, without assistance or review by a qualified human translator, that is text-based and provides instant translations (sometimes with audio I/O).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement to provide written translations via a qualified translator continues to apply. §92.201(c)(3) requires a human translator to review machine translation under certain circumstances (minimum requirement includes circumstances critical to one's rights or benefits). OCR will monitor technology and may issue future guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: National origin definition and related enforcement note
rubrics_metrics.description: National origin means a person's, or their ancestor's, place of origin or a person's manifestation of the physical, cultural, or linguistic characteristics of a national origin group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR recognizes intersections between national origin, LEP, race, and ethnicity and finalizes clarifying regulatory language addressing discrimination on multiple bases. Differential treatment such as requiring additional verification based on appearance, name, accent, LEP, or suspected immigration status may violate section 1557 and other civil rights laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of patient care decision support tool
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'patient care decision support tool' means any automated or non-automated tool, mechanism, method, technology, or combination used by a covered entity to support clinical decision-making in its health programs or activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rephrasing replaces 'clinical algorithm' and clarifies §92.210 applies to tools used for screening, risk prediction, diagnosis, prognosis, clinical decision-making, treatment planning, health care operations, allocation of resources, assessing health status, recommending care, disease management guidance, determining eligibility, and conducting utilization review related to patient care directed by a provider. The preamble notes there are examples of tools to which §92.210 does not apply discussed elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified bilingual/multilingual staff definition and assessment expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'qualified bilingual/multilingual staff' member is a workforce member designated by the covered entity to provide oral language assistance in the person's current job responsibilities who has demonstrated: (1) proficiency in speaking and understanding both spoken English and at least one other language (including specialized vocabulary), and (2) ability to effectively, accurately, and impartially communicate directly with individuals with LEP in their primary language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-identification alone is insufficient; covered entities should determine processes to assess and periodically assess qualifications. While such staff may also be qualified interpreters, interpreting is a separate skill and anyone serving as an interpreter must meet the independent definition of 'qualified interpreter for an individual with LEP.' OCR may provide future guidance/technical assistance and encourages training and compensation to support development and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified interpreter for an individual with a disability — alignment and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'qualified interpreter for an individual with a disability' must be able to interpret effectively, accurately, and impartially, both receptively and expressively, using any necessary specialized vocabulary; the definition is revised to align with the interpreter standards for individuals with LEP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters recommended including three parts used in the LEP interpreter definition: (1) demonstrated proficiency, (2) ability to interpret effectively/accurately/impartially, and (3) adherence to generally accepted interpreter ethics. OCR revised the definition for consistency. For sign language interpreters, proficiency should include speaking/understanding both English and the relevant sign language; CDIs should have specialized Deaf interpreting training; transliterators should demonstrate proficiency in relevant alternative communication modalities. Interpreters should convey without changes/omissions/additions and preserve tone, sentiment, and emotional level; adhere to recognized standards of practice and professional codes of ethics (e.g., NCICH, RID).
